purpose: adaptive white-box pilot: does the defense survive an attacker who knows it is there?

attack.init: seeded uniform(-eps, eps) per (seed, image id, restart); identical for the oblivious and the adaptive attack
attack.restart_selection: lowest surrogate objective on the quantized attack-frame tensor
attack.pixel_space: raw [0,1], native resolution, differentiable ultralytics letterbox into the model
attack.objective: minimize J = sum_anchors max_class pred[:,4:,:] (post-sigmoid confidences), i.e. maximize -J; untargeted, no ground truth, no self-labels, box regression excluded, no objectness term

surrogates.median: true a.e. gradient of the unfold median (each output routes to the input pixel its window selected)

bpda.forward: exact deployed value incl. uint8 round-trips; round-trips straight-through in the backward
bpda.eot: union-aware max: per anchor, max over the 3 branches of the max-class confidence, summed over anchors

implementation_uncertainty: Native space: the perturbation lives at native resolution, each surrogate defense runs there as deployed, and the model input is a differentiable copy of ultralytics' predict letterbox (minimum-rectangle padding to the stride, grey 114, centred). It resizes with torch bilinear where ultralytics uses cv2 INTER_LINEAR on uint8, so the two agree exactly when no resize is needed (longest side == 640) and differ by interpolation rounding otherwise (under 1/255 per pixel against ultralytics' LetterBox in tests/test_attack_units.py). The letterbox-vs-native scale mismatch of the default mode is removed and nothing resamples the perturbation after the attack. The uint8 output is clipped to the clean image +/- 7/255 (eps*255 = 7.65 is not whole, and truncation or rounding alone would move a pixel by 8/255), so no pixel the defense receives moves more than eps.
BPDA identity Jacobian (straight-through) for jpeg: the standard approximation, not the transform's true Jacobian; a learned differentiable proxy could give a stronger attacker.

True gradients: median: true a.e. gradient of the unfold median (each output routes to the input pixel its window selected); gaussian: true gradient. The median gradient is sparse (one input per output pixel), so it carries less signal per step than a smooth filter's.

Every surrogate forwards the deployed phase3_common transform's exact output on the attack-frame tensor (the native image), including the deployed pipeline's truncating uint8 round-trips (phase3_common.tensor_to_pil); those round-trips are straight-through in the backward pass. The attack output is converted to uint8 by truncation, the Phase-3 conversion: every perturbed pixel is floored, on average 0.5/255 below rounding.

EOT loss 'max' mirrors the NMS-union merge (a box survives if ANY branch keeps it) by suppressing the most confident branch per anchor. It is still a proxy: the real merge matches post-threshold boxes across branches by IoU, not anchors by index. Its gradient is exact: per anchor, only the winning branch's gradient counts (computed in one batched pass or branch by branch, per --eot-batch, equal up to float rounding).
EOT aggregates over deterministic defense branches, not over defense randomness (EnsJMG has none); a randomized defense would need EOT samples per branch as well.

PGD init: one seeded uniform(-eps, eps) draw per (seed, image id, restart), identical for the oblivious and the adaptive attack, so the two differ only in the gradient they follow. Phase 3 drew its init from the unseeded global RNG, so Phase-3 and Phase-4 attacked numbers also differ by init noise.

PGD iterate selection 'best': per restart, the last iterate and the lowest-objective iterate seen are both quantized and the one with the lower objective after quantization is kept (Phase 3 kept the last iterate). Applied to the oblivious and the adaptive attack alike.

surrogate_objective.definition: J = sum over anchors of the max-class confidence, measured THROUGH EnsJMG with the attack's own surrogate (deployed forward values, native frame, eot-loss max); lower = more suppression. A diagnostic of the attacker's optimisation, not a detection metric.
